stick_office.name: Stick Office
stick_office.description: A rod on a bench, and the question of where its office lives. TWO tokens declare an axis called office with identical values (reach | rule | lever | pointer | baton) - grab_long_stick and grab_rainbow_stick - and they cannot disagree about the word, because they are ONE SCRIPT: grab_long_stick.tscn:3 and grab_rainbow_stick.tscn:3 both ext_resource grab_rod.gd and both attach it to the root at :32. This is the corpus's most common hidden family found again, and for the first time there is a MEASUREMENT of it: both tokens were swept, and doc/reports/sweep_grab_long_stick_bite.json and sweep_grab_rainbow_stick_bite.json rank all ten office pairs in the same order and agree on every one to within 3.6 percent, five of the ten to within 1 percent. Two sheets, one experiment, run twice on the same code. The brief's second suspicion - that office names a USE and neither source changes any geometry - is DESTROYED on its first half and CONFIRMED on its second. grab_rod.gd builds real geometry for four of five values (a graduated bone blade :154-165, a sleeved effort arm with bands, collar and counterweight :179-187, a full-length graphite taper :199-202, an ivory sleeve with cork grip and brass pommel :215-221); reach builds nothing at all :120-123, correctly, because it is the shipped default across 45 live placements. But every fitting is added as ONE child of the rod (:142 add_child(dress)) and the rod is an XRToolsPickable RigidBody3D - so THE LEVER'S FULCRUM IS WELDED TO THE LEVER (:186, with its shim at :187), parented to the body that gets picked up, hanging 0.112 m below a shaft that can be held anywhere, touching nothing. A fulcrum is by definition the part of a lever that does not move with the lever. The author knew what the axis wanted and had exactly one node to put it on; the docstring concedes it at :27-28, 'what the rod is FOR ... shows entirely in what is fitted at its ends'. This bench keeps office with the family's five values in the family's order and the family's palette, copied as Colors from grab_rod.gd:150-152, 173-177, 195-197 and 210-213, and crosses it with reading, which is one question - WHERE DOES THE OFFICE LIVE - answered three ways: fitted (on the rod, the source's answer rebuilt to scale, wedge still hanging), apparatus (in the world; the rod is bare and byte-identical in all five cells and what changes is what stands around it), trace (in what was done; the rod is bare, the apparatus is gone, and what remains is the state the act left). Three of the fifteen frames are the same photograph, and that is the argument: reach-fitted is a bare rod because the source fits nothing to a reach, pointer-trace is a bare rod because grab_rod.gd:70 says 'It indicates; it does not touch', baton-trace is a bare rod because :208-209 says 'it touches nothing'. One picture, three answers, and the source wrote two of the three reasons itself.
dev_themes: an office is a relation, not a shape
a two-member family that is one script, measured twice
the fulcrum is welded to the lever
two of five offices act on people and leave no evidence
interactions: walk the office axis in the fitted reading. This is the source family's entire behaviour, rebuilt at a scale a camera can read, and reach is a bare rod because grab_rod.gd:120-123 builds nothing for it. Look at the lever cell: the wedge hangs in mid-air with 0.130 m of clear space between its base and the bench. That gap is grab_rod.gd:186 drawn at 1:1, and it is the whole finding.

compare fitted-lever against apparatus-lever. Same wedge, same silhouette, same colour; the only difference is that one of them reaches the ground. A fulcrum in contact with the world and a fulcrum hanging off the lever are two different physics and one axis value, and the source can only build the second.

walk the office axis in the apparatus reading and watch the ROD not move. All five cells carry the identical shaft, grip and bead - the office is entirely in the shelf, the scale board, the standing fulcrum and its load, the target card and the fitted case. If a still can tell these five apart, and it can, then the office was never a property of the rod.

walk the office axis in the trace reading and count what is there. Three cells carry evidence (the retrieved thing and its drag scuff, the ruled stock, the displaced load and the crushed bite) and two carry nothing at all. That is not a gap in the bench; it is the vocabulary splitting in half. reach, rule and lever act on surfaces; pointer and baton act on people. office is two axes wearing one word, and this is the only column in the programme where the split can be photographed.

find the three identical frames. reach-fitted, pointer-trace and baton-trace are the same picture for three different reasons, two of which the source states in its own comments. They are registered as designed nulls, so if any pair of them differs the bench is broken rather than interesting.
stick_office.capacity: SEE that an affordance is a relation between a body and a world, and that an artifact which can only build one of the two terms will weld the missing term onto the one it has - then see the cost, which is a fulcrum that travels with the lever and a vocabulary in which two of five values leave nothing behind

dna.default: office=reach, reading=fitted. BOTH DEFAULTS ARE THE SOURCE'S. grab_rod.gd:79 ships office = "reach" and :120-123 builds nothing for it, which is correct and deliberate: 45 live placements (28 grab_long_stick, 17 grab_rainbow_stick, counted across commons/maps) carry no config at all, so every one of them is the legacy body byte for byte and the axis has never been met in a map. reading=fitted is the other half of the same shipped state: fitted is WHERE THE SOURCE PUTS THE OFFICE, on the rod. So the default cell of this bench is a bare rod on a bench - the thing being argued with, photographed first - and every other cell is a step away from it.
dna.was: TWO REGISTRY TOKENS, TWO SCENES, ONE SCRIPT, AND FOR ONCE A MEASUREMENT OF IT. grab_long_stick.tscn and grab_rainbow_stick.tscn are identical node for node and transform for transform: the same pickable.tscn instance, the same 0.169 m grip block at x=-0.608, the same 1.5 m cylinder along X, the same 0.05 m lit bead at x=1.003, the same MesmerizingTrail targeting that bead. Both name grab_rod.gd at :3 and attach it at :32. They differ only in dressing - magenta grip and a long_cloth trail on one (:24, :36), dark metallic grip and a rainbow trail on the other, and 2 to 3 mm of shaft radius (:26, top/bottom 0.010/0.011 against 0.012/0.014). Their loudest difference, the trail, is a RATE and is invisible to a still: MesmerizingTrail needs two recorded points before it builds a mesh, which grab_rod.gd:76-78 already says. The two bite reports prove the rest: reach-rule 0.370 against 0.357, reach-lever 0.401 against 0.398, reach-pointer 0.361 against 0.348, reach-baton 0.465 against 0.464, rule-lever 0.626 against 0.614, rule-pointer 0.505 against 0.495, rule-baton 0.557 against 0.557, lever-pointer 0.478 against 0.462, lever-baton 0.663 against 0.659, pointer-baton 0.504 against 0.503. Identical rank order, mean disagreement 1.6 percent. When a shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE - and these do, which is exactly why they are worth nothing as independent evidence about the word.
dna.note: THE INSTRUMENT DECISIONS, EACH ONE COSTING SOMETHING. (1) THE ASSEMBLY IS YAWED 0.62 rad. capture_config_sweep.gd:69 sets YAW 0.62 and :443 builds the camera direction as Vector3(sin(yaw)cos(pitch), -sin(pitch), cos(yaw)cos(pitch)), whose horizontal bearing is atan2(sin 0.62, cos 0.62) = 0.62 exactly. Rotating the rig by the same angle puts the rod's axis PERPENDICULAR to that bearing, so a 1.4 m rod photographs at full length instead of foreshortened, and marks laid along it are unforeshortened too. It costs the bench TOP, which is a horizontal plane seen at 14.9 degrees and therefore compressed by sin(0.26) = 0.2571 to a band 0.1131 m tall, 43 px of the 760. Every trace is designed long in X and shallow in Z for that reason, and it is the reason the trace column is the quietest on the sheet. (2) THERE IS A CONSTANT AABB ANCHOR. Anchor is a 1.680 x 0.560 x 0.460 BoxMesh with layers = 0 - invisible, still counted, because capture_config_sweep.gd:1488 merges every MeshInstance3D regardless of layer or visibility. Without it the camera would retreat for the tall apparatus cells and close in for the flat trace cells and every measured pair would carry a framing change it did not earn; with it the camera stands still across all fifteen. (3) dna.framing IS 0.48 AND IT IS THE REASON THIS BENCH EXISTS. The two sources fit by DIAGONAL: a 1.74 x 0.10 x 0.10 m rod has a 1.746 m diagonal and about 0.005 m2 of silhouette, so both sweeps measured a subject at 2.255 and 2.273 percent of frame and both were reported 'faint - under 2 percent of the frame moved'. Inside the subject, lever against baton moved 0.663/2.255 = 29.4 percent of the rod. The verdict on the family's own axis was a fact about the camera; neither registry entry carries a framing hint. (4) EVERYTHING IS LIT, NOT UNSHADED. This is a geometry axis, not a colour axis, so shading is signal here rather than noise - and it is why the prediction below is a FLOOR: shadows, contact darkening and antialiasing all add differing pixels that a paper area calculation cannot see. (5) NO NUMERIC VALUE IN EITHER AXIS. Both are word enums typed String, so cabinet_sweep.coerce() has nothing to numericise and the tier_terrarium failure - Object.set() refusing a typed property in silence - cannot occur. Checked, not assumed. (6) DETERMINISTIC. No RandomNumberGenerator, no randf, no noise, no _process, no Timer, no tween, no shader; the scuff arc is a closed-form parabola in the loop index. Two builds are the same bytes, which is what makes the three nulls identities rather than near-misses, and it is why no dna.fixture is needed.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: rule against pointer, in the trace reading (equivalently rule against baton, which is the same frame)
predicted_degeneracy.metric: changed_pct, frame percent - the sweep's default pixel COUNT over the whole 760x760 frame. This is an AREA prediction, not a magnitude one: the claim is how much of the frame gains an object, not how far any pixel moves in luma, so the counting metric is the right one and the word 'luma' is deliberately not written here. The stock is Color(0.80,0.75,0.63) on a bench of Color(0.34,0.31,0.27), about 100 grey levels apart, so no differing pixel is anywhere near a threshold.
predicted_degeneracy.floor_or_two_sided: FLOOR. Everything on this bench is lit with the rig's default key, so the stock sheet will also darken the bench where it sits, soften its own edges under antialiasing, and gain a specular roll on its top face - none of which a flat area calculation can see. The sheet also sits at local z = +0.060, nearer the camera than the AABB centre the frame is scaled at, so perspective makes it slightly larger than the orthographic figure. Every term points the same way. A sweep landing BELOW 0.843 percent means something is broken - the framing hint was dropped, the anchor stopped pinning the camera, or the trace builder did not run - and should be investigated before the number is read as a fact about the axis. The historical under-shoot factor on geometry predictions in this programme is 1.5x to 6.7x.
predicted_degeneracy.pool: the TEN office pairs inside the trace reading, ranked among themselves. Not the 105 pairs of the sheet. The smallest of the ten is the designed null (pointer against baton, 0.000 percent), so this is the smallest NON-NULL of the ten. The full predicted ordering of that pool: pointer-baton 0.000, rule-pointer 0.843, rule-baton 0.843, lever-pointer 1.124, lever-baton 1.124, reach-pointer 1.258, reach-baton 1.258, rule-lever 1.967, reach-rule 2.100, reach-lever 2.382.
predicted_degeneracy.why: A RULE REMOVES NOTHING AND MOVES NOTHING. It is the only contact office on the sheet whose entire product is a mark it let something else make, so its trace is the thinnest evidence any of the three acting offices can leave, and pointer's trace is nothing at all. The difference between the two frames is therefore exactly one object: the stock. ARITHMETIC. The stock is a box 0.760 x 0.006 x 0.150 lying on the bench top; the scribed line, the eleven ruled ticks and the datum are drawn ON its top face and add no silhouette. The rig is yawed 0.62 rad so the stock's long axis is perpendicular to the camera bearing and unforeshortened, and the camera is pitched 0.26 rad, so the top face projects by sin(0.26) = 0.2570806 and the front edge by cos(0.26) = 0.9663900. TOP: 0.760 x 0.150 x 0.2570806 = 0.0293072 m2. FRONT EDGE: 0.760 x 0.006 x 0.9663900 = 0.0044067 m2. The two end faces lie in the camera's own bearing plane and project to zero. TOTAL 0.0337139 m2. FRAME: the anchor gives a world AABB of 1.6345912 x 0.560000 x 1.3505226 (the 1.680 x 0.560 x 0.460 local box rotated 0.62 about Y: half-x = 0.840 cos 0.62 + 0.230 sin 0.62 = 0.8172956, half-z = 0.840 sin 0.62 + 0.230 cos 0.62 = 0.6752613), diagonal 2.1930343, radius 1.0965172. capture_config_sweep.gd:442 sets dist = radius / tan(17 deg) x 1.9 x 0.48 = 3.270903 m, so the frame is a square of side 2 x radius x 1.9 x 0.48 = 2.000041 m, area 4.000164 m2. RESULT: 0.0337139 / 4.000164 = 0.00842814 = 0.843 percent, which is 4868 of the 577600 pixels. OCCLUSION CHECKED: the stock's frame-vertical offset from the rod is about -0.257 m against a rod half-thickness of 0.016, so it is nowhere behind the shaft; and it sits 0.048 m above the bench's own front-top edge in frame, so the bench lip does not cut it. NOT OCCLUDED, NOT CLIPPED.
predicted_degeneracy.twin: THE SAME NUMBER APPEARS TWICE ON THE SHEET AND THAT IS A FREE CONSISTENCY CHECK. reach-fitted against rule-trace must also measure 0.843 percent, because reach-fitted and pointer-trace are a designed null - the same picture. If the two pairs disagree by more than render noise, the null is broken and the whole sheet is suspect, and the disagreement will say so before any human looks at a tile.
predicted_degeneracy.peak_for_contrast: The predicted loudest pair is fitted-lever against apparatus-baton, at roughly 6 percent of frame: a welded wedge with a counterweight and a sleeved effort arm against a bare rod above an open fitted case. The headline is a peak, so it is written down here next to the floor: the ratio between them is about 7x, and any report quoting only the peak has said nothing about the trace column, which is where this bench's argument actually lives.

dna.predicted_relationship: TWO CLAIMS THAT DO NOT NEED A PERCENTAGE TO BE WRONG. FIRST: the apparatus column must be the LOUDEST of the three readings and the fitted column the second, even though the fitted column is the only one where the rod itself changes. The mechanism is area - a shelf on a post, a 1.300 x 0.320 scale board, a standing fulcrum with a 0.200 x 0.240 x 0.180 load, a target card on a stand and an open case are each 0.03 to 0.09 m2 of frontal silhouette, while the largest fitting on the rod (the lever's dressing) is under 0.05 m2 and most are under 0.03. If the fitted column beats the apparatus column, the anchor is not pinning the camera. SECOND, AND IT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE VOCABULARY RATHER THAN THE BENCH: within the trace reading the five offices will sort into a group of three and a group of two with nothing between them - reach, rule and lever between 0.8 and 2.4 percent against each other and against the empty cells, pointer and baton at exactly 0.000. There is no intermediate value and there cannot be one, because the split is not a matter of degree. That gap is the evidence that office is two axes wearing one word.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, TO THE BYTE, AND THE SOURCE WROTE BOTH REASONS. _read_trace() falls through to `pass` for pointer and for baton, so each cell is the standing bench and nothing else: the same anchor, bench, two posts, shaft, grip and bead, at the same transforms, with the same materials, built by the same deterministic code with no randomness and no _process. The two PNGs are the same file. The justification is not this bench's - grab_rod.gd:70 says of the pointer 'It indicates; it does not touch', and :208-209 says of the baton 'a baton is held and shown, and it touches nothing'. WHAT THIS NULL SAYS: a still camera pointed at the world cannot tell a pointer from a baton, because neither of them does anything to the world. Anything above 0.15 percent is render nondeterminism. Anything above 1 percent means a trace builder is running for a value that has none, and the trace column's whole argument is then a fact about a bug.

IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND CROSS-AXIS ON PURPOSE - this is the sharpest sentence the sheet can say. _read_fitted() falls through to `pass` for reach, reproducing grab_rod.gd:120-123 exactly ('reach - the bare shaft. Nothing is fitted, so nothing is built'); _read_trace() falls through to `pass` for pointer. Two different axes, two different readings, two entirely different reasons, one photograph. THE ARGUMENT: a bare rod is what you get when the office is not in the rod AND the act left no mark, and no camera can distinguish those two absences. That is what it means for a word to name a use rather than a shape - and it is unsayable inside the source family, where reading does not exist and reach-with-nothing-fitted is simply the shipped default. Anything above 0.15 percent is render nondeterminism. Anything above 1 percent means either reach is building a fitting or pointer is building a trace.

THE THIRD EDGE OF THE SAME TRIANGLE, registered rather than left to transitivity, because a three-way identity that is only checked twice can hide one broken cell. reach-fitted builds nothing (grab_rod.gd:120-123), baton-trace builds nothing (:208-209). If the first two nulls hold and this one does not, the fault is in the comparison harness rather than in the artifact, which is a distinction worth being able to make without opening a PNG.

dna.designed_nulls_why: THREE NULLS, AND THEY ARE THE SAME NULL: three of the fifteen cells are one photograph. That is a fifth of the sheet spent on nothing, deliberately, and it is where the argument is. In the source family the bare rod is a single fact - reach, the default, the thing 45 placements ship. Crossed with a reading axis it turns out to be the answer to three separate questions, two of which are about offices the source itself declares non-contact in its own comments. A vocabulary in which one picture answers three questions is not a vocabulary about the pictured thing. WHY NO NULL IS CONDITIONED ON ANYTHING ELSE: both nulls-by-parameter that suggested themselves (pinning a fixture, freezing a seed) were unavailable and unnecessary - this bench has no random source and no dna.fixture - so all three are conditioned only on the two swept axes, which is the condition wave 21 found violated elsewhere.
dna.kin: GRAB_STICK IS THE THIRD SIBLING AND IT IS NOT IN THE FAMILY, which is worth recording because it looks like it should be. commons/primitives/cubes/grab_stick.tscn is the same pickable body with the same grip block and the same trail rig, but its root runs grab_cube.gd (:4), not grab_rod.gd, so it declares no axis and has 2 live placements; a fourth token named grab_stick in color.json points at a different scene entirely (algorithms/color/color_scanner/grab_stick.tscn). The office family is exactly two names. THE WORD `reading` IS THE HOUSE SLOT for a synthesis's second axis - 37 artifacts declare it, each with its own values - and it is used here in that sense and no other. THE WORDS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: `apparatus` is already an AXIS NAME on durer_scene, so it appears here only as a VALUE, where it cannot collide; `duty` (curation_station) and `custody` (pick_up_cube) are both near neighbours of `office` in ordinary English and both mean something else in this corpus, so neither was borrowed. `evidence` was the first choice for the second axis and was dropped: 50 artifacts declare it, it is the closest thing this corpus has to a reserved word, and taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary.
declines: THE HAND. Every office in this vocabulary is completed by a hand, and the baton's is completed by two - a baton is defined by being handed on. No hand is modelled. A hand at this scale would be the largest object in at least three cells, its pose would become the loudest variable on the sheet, and the reader would be measuring a gesture rather than an apparatus. The absence is the reason the baton's apparatus is its CASE rather than its recipient: custody is the part of a hand-off that holds still to be photographed. Named here rather than faked.

A SIXTH OFFICE. A rod is also a whip, a spit, an axle, an oar, a vaulting pole, a splint and a weapon, and none of those is in grab_rod.gd:80. The five values here are the source's five, in the source's order, with the source's palette. A sixth would have made the sheet a fact about this bench's taste in tools rather than about a family's declared vocabulary.

AN ALL-RUNGS READING. A fourth value - call it `complete`, the rod fitted AND the apparatus standing AND the trace on the bench - was considered and refused. It is exactly the shape wave 20 found six times in the corpus and wave 21 three more: a value that is the union of the others, which always photographs as the loudest cell and always says nothing, because every pixel in it belongs to some other value. Recorded as refused rather than merely absent, so the next reader knows it was seen.

A `hand` READING (in the hand, as opposed to on the rod / in the world / in the mark). It is a real fourth place for an office to live and it is the one the source's XR body actually implements - grab_rod.gd inherits pickup, grab points and snapping from grab_cube.gd unchanged. It is declined for the reason above (no hand) and for a second: the reading axis is one question, WHERE IS THE OFFICE, and answering it with three places in the world plus one in the body would make it two questions in one word.

THE TRAILS. Both sources' most conspicuous feature is a motion trail - long_cloth.gdshader on one, rainbow_trail.gdshader on the other, both driven by MesmerizingTrail off the lit bead. It is the ONLY loud difference between the two tokens and it is invisible to a still: the trail needs two recorded points before it builds a mesh at all, which grab_rod.gd:76-78 states. Not built here. Worth saying plainly: the thing that makes a rainbow stick a rainbow stick cannot be photographed, so the difference between the two members of this family is unphotographable, and the sameness is measured.

MOVING THE ROD. In three of the five fitted cells the source's arrangement only makes physical sense if the rod is off the bench and in the air - a lever pivots, a pointer is raised, a baton is carried. The rod is left resting on its two posts in all fifteen cells anyway, because a rod at a different height in different cells changes the AABB, moves the camera, and makes every measured pair carry a framing difference it did not earn. The cost is that the fitted-lever cell shows a fulcrum hanging over a bench it does not touch, which happens to be exactly what grab_rod.gd builds, so the compromise and the finding are the same picture.
dna.sweep_note: --max=15 IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE DEFAULT WOULD CUT THE SHEET IN HALF. build_dna_gallery caps the cross product and trims the LATER axis from the tail; at the default --max=9 a 5 x 3 sheet renders as 5 x 1, which keeps office whole and deletes apparatus and trace - the two readings that carry the argument, both predictions and all three designed nulls. The declared order is office first, reading second, so it is reading that gets cut. This is the same trap recorded against every previous multi-axis sweep in this programme.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE WORLD BOX IS A CONSTANT IN ALL FIFTEEN CELLS AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ANCHOR. A 1.680 x 0.560 x 0.460 BoxMesh with layers = 0 sits at local (0, 0.280, 0); it renders nothing and is merged into the capture AABB anyway, because capture_config_sweep.gd:1488 takes every MeshInstance3D without asking about layer or visibility. Everything built stays inside it: the grip ends at x = -0.810 and the reach shelf at x = +0.800 against an anchor half-width of 0.840; the tallest thing in any cell is the reach shelf's object at y = 0.548 against an anchor height of 0.560; the deepest are the scale board at z = -0.176 and the case lid at z = -0.077 against an anchor half-depth of 0.230. The whole rig is yawed 0.62 rad about Y to meet the sweep's standpoint, which is what makes the world box 1.635 wide rather than 1.680; a map placing this artifact should expect the bench to stand 35.5 degrees off the grid axis, or pass its own rotation in the token.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry from the file's own constants; no Godot was run. The Anchor box has local half-extents (0.840, 0.280, 0.230) and is rotated 0.62 rad about Y, giving half-x = 0.840 cos 0.62 + 0.230 sin 0.62 = 0.8172956 and half-z = 0.840 sin 0.62 + 0.230 cos 0.62 = 0.6752613; height is unaffected by a yaw, so the box runs from the floor to 0.560 and its centre sits at 0.280. Diagonal 2.1930343, radius 1.0965172, and at dna.framing 0.48 the sweep stands at 3.270903 m with a 2.000041 m frame: the assembly's 1.680 m span fills 84.0 percent of the frame width, leaving 0.160 m of margin each side, so nothing clips. The rod alone is 1.570 m of that span and is photographed at its full length because it lies perpendicular to the camera bearing.
